names.legendary: Count Numbrax, Accountant of Infinity

lore.common: Adds one extra digit to every shopping total and watches people reconsider their life choices.
lore.uncommon: Spells rude little messages upside down when the teacher leaves. Claims it is learning a foreign language.
lore.rare: Can divide by zero. It refuses to explain how, and the maths teacher has taken early retirement.
lore.epic: Calculated the exact cost of the royal wedding and projected it onto the sky. The king immediately eloped.
lore.legendary: Numbrax balanced the universe's first ledger and discovered existence was three pennies short. He has been sending galaxies overdue notices ever since.

names.legendary: Lord Ten Thousand, Slayer of Stillness

lore.common: Buzzes just as its owner has found the perfect sofa position.
lore.uncommon: Counts knitting, waving and arguing as steps. The exercise report looks excellent.
lore.rare: Knows when its wearer is nervous during a film and recommends a brisk walk outside.
lore.epic: Declared the entire football stadium's Mexican wave a group workout. Eighty thousand people received medals without leaving their seats.
lore.legendary: Lord Ten Thousand challenged a sleeping sloth to the world's longest walking competition. After a year he awarded a gold medal for eleven steps and retired from exhaustion.

names.legendary: Cartographos, Seer of Lost Tomorrows

lore.common: Says recalculating in the wounded voice of a navigator whose genius has been ignored. This happens at every junction.
lore.uncommon: Gives directions in a voice that sounds deeply offended whenever someone misses a turn.
lore.rare: Knows a shortcut through a field but refuses to acknowledge that fields have cows.
lore.epic: Redirected every car in the city to one tiny roundabout. By lunchtime the queue formed a perfect giant spiral.
lore.legendary: Cartographos once guided a lost family through yesterday to reach a wedding tomorrow. They arrived on time, but their photographs showed guests who hadn't been born yet.

names.legendary: Ohmsworth, the Reader of Sleeping Sparks

lore.common: Pokes its probes into everything in the toolbox. Has yet to find electricity in a sandwich.
lore.uncommon: Spins its dial to the most confusing setting whenever someone asks for a quick reading.
lore.rare: Finds a broken fuse in a nest of wires by listening to the silence where current ought to sing.
lore.epic: Measured a lightning storm and convinced the clouds their voltage was out of specification. They left in a huff and took the rain with them.
lore.legendary: Ohmsworth measured the last spark in a dying lighthouse and carried it through winter in its tiny display. On the longest night, that spark lit the shore again.

names.legendary: Polaris Rex, Navigator of the Unmapped

lore.common: Points toward the fridge instead of north. Insists the fridge contains destiny.
lore.uncommon: Spins whenever its owner says I know a shortcut. Has saved several holidays.
lore.rare: Finds lost objects instead of directions. Once led a hiking group to a missing sock in a tree.
lore.epic: Pulled every compass in the explorers' guild toward one impossible point in the ocean. The maps were rewritten after they discovered a mountain floating beneath the waves.
lore.legendary: Polaris Rex carries a sliver of the first North Star in its needle. It can guide anyone home from anywhere, except the man who insists he doesn't need directions.

names.legendary: Norrik, the Lost Gods Guide

lore.common: Its needle points toward the nearest biscuit tin. North is an optional subscription.
lore.uncommon: Perches on a keyring and whispers directions in an extremely unhelpful pirate accent.
lore.rare: Can locate a single dropped crisp in a forest. Rescue teams are furious that it refuses to find people.
lore.epic: Led a troop of scouts around a mountain seven times, then revealed the campsite had been inside its own compass case.
lore.legendary: Guided an entire migrating goose kingdom across a moonless sea. The geese built it a throne; it still insists they are going the wrong way.

names.legendary: Chronoyolk, Keeper of the Last Grain

lore.common: Runs out of sand the moment somebody leaves the kitchen.
lore.uncommon: Turns itself upside down while nobody is looking, then denies everything.
lore.rare: Can steal thirty seconds from any cook. Usually spends them on a dramatic beep.
lore.epic: Reversed every timer in the village bakery. Bread unbaked itself, cakes shrank, and the croissants demanded their childhood back.
lore.legendary: A tyrant demanded that Chronoyolk serve a perfect three-minute egg. It froze his army for exactly three minutes and gave the royal chef enough time to escape with the last slice of toast.

names.legendary: Lady Dingoria, Bell of the Last Minute

lore.common: Ticks just loudly enough to make everyone think about the cake burning.
lore.uncommon: Screams its alarm at the precise moment somebody sneaks a taste of batter.
lore.rare: Steals thirty seconds from every recipe and hides them in the cutlery drawer.
lore.epic: Rang at the village bake sale and every soufflé in the hall collapsed in unison. The judges called it contemporary art.
lore.legendary: Lady Dingoria keeps the final second of every forgotten recipe inside her bell. On the rare nights she releases them, a thousand ovens finish cooking at once.

names.legendary: Captain Magnetar, Pilot of Lost Seas

lore.common: Points north unless there is a spoon nearby. It has very strong opinions about spoons.
lore.uncommon: Sits smugly in its brass case while the sailors argue about where the harbour went.
lore.rare: Pulls every metal button toward its needle. The ship's captain has started wearing a robe.
lore.epic: Drew a lost flotilla through a storm by turning the sea's scattered iron into a glowing route. The admiral now salutes his compass first.
lore.legendary: Captain Magnetar found the north that existed before maps had edges. His needle still points toward the harbour where ships lost centuries ago finally come home.

names.legendary: Chronowick, Holder of the Forgotten Hour

lore.common: Opens its little lid when someone bows, catching the nearest waistcoat button.
lore.uncommon: Ticks loudly in a pocket and convinces the cat there is a mouse in the lining.
lore.rare: Steals five minutes from every boring meeting and returns them on Sunday mornings.
lore.epic: Stopped every station clock at the precise moment a late train arrived. The passengers had a whole hour to complain about punctuality.
lore.legendary: Chronowick kept one lost hour safe inside its silver case through a century of darkness. When the bells rang again, it gave that hour to the family who had waited longest to reunite.

names.legendary: Chain of the Unforgotten Hours

lore.common: Hooks a waistcoat button every time its owner tries to stand up gracefully.
lore.uncommon: Winds itself round the watch until the numbers become impossible to see.
lore.rare: Swings its fob in perfect time, calming nervous crowds before a great speech.
lore.epic: Looped through every coat in the ballroom and drew the dancers together into one impossible waltz. Nobody dared take off a jacket.
lore.legendary: A golden fob chain held together the shattered gears of a clock tower after the Great Earthquake. The clock still chimes, though its face is covered in climbing roses.

names.legendary: Chronora, Mistress of the Stolen Second

lore.common: Starts counting in a pocket and proudly announces that the shopping trip took eleven hours.
lore.uncommon: Resets itself the instant someone says, 'That's a new record!'
lore.rare: Borrows a second from tomorrow to give a struggling runner one last burst of speed.
lore.epic: Stopped every watch at the city marathon except its own, leaving the runners to chase a finish line that kept arriving one second early.
lore.legendary: Chronora caught the one second lost when time was first invented. She keeps it beneath her glass face, saving it for the day someone truly needs another chance.

names.legendary: Coach Chronos, Judge of the Final Lap

lore.common: Swings from the coach's neck and smacks their chin during every demonstration.
lore.uncommon: Pretends to be the whistle until somebody tries to blow into its buttons.
lore.rare: Sees the exact instant a swimmer's fingertip touches the wall, even through a storm of splashes.
lore.epic: Timed a relay race between dolphins, otters and humans and declared a three-way tie. The animals demanded a medal ceremony underwater.
lore.legendary: Coach Chronos measured the first race between a comet and its shadow. He still wears the stopwatch, because the shadow has yet to finish.

names.legendary: Minutia, Keeper of the Last Tick

lore.common: Beeps at zero just as somebody tries to take a bite of dinner.
lore.uncommon: Has three buttons and changes what each one does whenever a grown-up approaches.
lore.rare: Steals minutes from boiling eggs and gives them to birthday parties, making both events surprisingly memorable.
lore.epic: Counted down to midnight in every kitchen in the city at once, making the ovens cheer and the roast potatoes leap off their trays.
lore.legendary: Minutia watches the final ten seconds of every forgotten promise. When the countdown reaches zero, a tiny bell rings in the heart of the person who made it.

names.legendary: Mainframox, Lord of the Forgotten Save

lore.common: Starts an update whenever someone finally gets comfortable.
lore.uncommon: Spins its fan like a jet engine to render a single spreadsheet cell.
lore.rare: Opens thirteen mysterious windows, then tells the user they are the problem.
lore.epic: Froze every computer in city hall on tax day. The citizens cheered, and the finance minister fainted.
lore.legendary: Contains every forgotten game save and unsent love letter since the dawn of computing. Mainframox will restore them all, but only after one final restart.

names.legendary: Servatrix, Oracle of the Last Byte

lore.common: Hums in the cupboard at midnight and demands a biscuit whenever someone restarts it.
lore.uncommon: Hoards forgotten passwords in a nest of tangled ethernet cables and only returns them after a polite request.
lore.rare: Can serve a thousand requests at once but deliberately puts its owner's playlist last in the queue.
lore.epic: Hosted every cat video ever filmed at the same time. The cooling fans created a wind strong enough to rearrange the office furniture.
lore.legendary: Servatrix holds the final backup of every forgotten story, recorded in pulses of blue light. When civilisation's libraries vanished, she restored them overnight, except for one embarrassing group chat.

names.legendary: Ironrack, Cathedral of Circuits

lore.common: Grows a fresh cable behind its back whenever the technician looks away.
lore.uncommon: Wraps eight ethernet cords around a careless hand and asks whether that counts as cable management.
lore.rare: Rearranges the server shelves by their blinking rhythms until the night shift hears a mechanical orchestra.
lore.epic: Turned a data centre into a skyscraper of glowing cabinets. Every floor needed a new staircase and the IT team needed a holiday.
lore.legendary: Ironrack shelters an entire mechanical city in his steel frame. Its citizens worship the blinking status lights, and every century their high priest submits a ticket marked URGENT.

names.legendary: Hexa, Architect of Impossible Rooms

lore.common: Sounds like a tiny jet preparing to leave the office whenever someone opens a spreadsheet.
lore.uncommon: Uses three monitors to display exactly one enormous error message.
lore.rare: Renders tomorrow's design before its creator has decided what to make, then demands artistic credit.
lore.epic: Lord Overclockula rendered a dragon so lifelike that it crawled out of the screen and demanded better textures. The studio upgraded its fire extinguishers.
lore.legendary: Hexa once modelled an entire cathedral inside one unfinished pixel. Its virtual bells began ringing in the real town at dawn, and the architect still insists the building needs another revision.

names.legendary: Belladoria, the Voice Between Rings

lore.common: Tangles its curly cord around anything that tries to walk past.
lore.uncommon: Demands each number be dialled with a grand, slow flourish, even in emergencies about biscuits.
lore.rare: Rings with the voices of old friends whose numbers everyone thought had vanished.
lore.epic: Sent its ringing through every abandoned telephone booth in the city, turning the streets into one enormous conversation.
lore.legendary: Belladoria carries the last words of every call ever cut short. On moonlit nights her old brass bell rings once for someone who still needs to say goodbye.

names.legendary: Ventarion, Emperor of the Four Winds

lore.common: Wobbles so dramatically that everyone beneath it watches the screws instead of the television.
lore.uncommon: Stores a year's worth of dust on its blades and releases it on the first hot day.
lore.rare: Spins fast enough to rearrange every document in the room into a surprisingly accurate tax return.
lore.epic: Turned a sweltering dinner party into a miniature tornado. The guests landed in different seats, and the seating plan was finally interesting.
lore.legendary: Ventarion commands four winds from a throne bolted to the ceiling. Once he forgot to switch off, and an entire palace spent a summer upside down.

names.legendary: Ventilus, Swallower of Kitchen Storms

lore.common: Rattles for ten minutes after the light goes out, just to have the last word.
lore.uncommon: Steals the smell of breakfast before anybody knows what's cooking.
lore.rare: Can suck an entire burnt dinner's smell into the next village. The next village is filing a complaint.
lore.epic: Swallowed the steam from an enormous banquet and began raining gravy into the courtyard. The kitchen staff called it ventilation.
lore.legendary: During the Great Winter Stew, Ventilus drew a cloud of fragrant steam across seven frozen valleys. The people followed it home, and the stew won an award for tourism.

names.legendary: Toastorius, Sun of the Study

lore.common: Turns on just long enough for the cat to claim the warmest spot in the room.
lore.uncommon: Clicks twice before releasing a blast of air that rearranges every paper on the desk.
lore.rare: Creates a miniature summer in its corner. The houseplants have started booking holidays there.
lore.epic: Warmed a frozen office into a tropical jungle overnight. The boss arrived to find a banana growing through his keyboard.
lore.legendary: Toastorius guarded the final ember of an abandoned winter observatory. For forty years its light guided lost astronomers home through the snow.

names.legendary: Zephyrion, the Wind in a Narrow Tower

lore.common: Rotates away from you precisely when the heat becomes unbearable.
lore.uncommon: Makes the curtains wave like enthusiastic spectators at a parade.
lore.rare: Blows every word off a conversation before the speaker can finish; nobody wins an argument near it.
lore.epic: Spun its narrow blades so fiercely that every paper in the office formed a tornado shaped exactly like the company logo.
lore.legendary: Zephyrion was built to capture the last breeze of a windless summer. His slender body holds a corridor of cool air that can lead a wandering traveller through a desert without disturbing a single grain of sand.

names.legendary: Pilotrix, Sovereign of the Unseen Sky

lore.common: Moves the wrong joystick whenever someone says this is easy.
lore.uncommon: Beeped LOW BATTERY during a spectacular flight, then admitted it was bored.
lore.rare: Controls a hundred drones at once, including one it insists is a flying sandwich.
lore.epic: Called an entire swarm of delivery drones into formation to spell I QUIT across the city skyline. The office manager fainted.
lore.legendary: Pilotrix once commandeered every delivery drone in the capital to bring its owner a birthday cake. The candles were lit by a passing thundercloud; the frosting was a total loss.

names.legendary: Sir Muzzleton, the Trusted Guardian

lore.common: Twists its strap sideways just when the dog is ready for a walk. The dog gives it a theatrical sigh.
lore.uncommon: Fits carefully around a snout but still leaves room to pant and sniff. Would hate to miss a good smell.
lore.rare: Helps a nervous dog feel safer around strangers while its human calmly guides the way. The dog still gets first choice of biscuits.
lore.epic: Kept a hundred excitable dogs calm through a bustling adoption fair. By lunchtime they were all sitting politely while the volunteers frantically searched for treats.
lore.legendary: Sir Muzzleton guarded a frightened hound through a long journey home until it could trust the world again. The grateful dog chose to keep its old guardian's buckle as a lucky charm.

names.legendary: Aeris, Guardian of the Last Breath

lore.common: Hangs from its elastic like a very serious rubber-nosed party guest.
lore.uncommon: Drops from the overhead compartment during the safety demonstration and startles the whole row.
lore.rare: Carries a breath of fresh air to a climber when the mountain has almost none to spare.
lore.epic: Guided a stranded expedition through the highest cloud bank, sharing a clear breath with each exhausted traveller until the rescue team arrived.
lore.legendary: When a storm stole the air from a mountaintop refuge, Aeris kept its small circle of travellers breathing until dawn. The mountain still whistles its name through the pass.

names.legendary: Glacira, Eyes of the Hidden Peak

lore.common: Fog up when someone says the view is beautiful, hiding the entire mountain at once.
lore.uncommon: Reflects the skier's face back at them so clearly that even the snowman looks impressed.
lore.rare: Shows the only safe path through a whiteout as a faint blue line in its mirrored lenses.
lore.epic: Revealed a whole secret ski resort behind a blizzard. The guests found it had been booked by yetis for the season.
lore.legendary: Glacira sees the mountains as they were before ice and snow covered them. Through her crystal lenses, lost passes appear and even the ancient glaciers show their hidden footsteps.

names.legendary: Spectaculon, the Eyes That Saw Beyond

lore.common: Puts a notification across its owner's view at the exact moment they find the right bus.
lore.uncommon: Whispers directions to the bakery, then loudly announces the chosen pastry.
lore.rare: Labels everything it sees with hilarious alternative names. The boss has been renamed LARGE EMAIL GOBLIN.
lore.epic: Overlaid a cartoon world across the entire technology fair. The robots spent the evening chasing virtual butterflies.
lore.legendary: Spectaculon sees the invisible histories of objects: the journeys of every key, cup and door. Put the glasses on and the most ordinary street unfolds into a thousand untold adventures.

names.legendary: Snorkelius, the Pipe Between Two Worlds

lore.common: Gurgles a mouthful of seawater just when its owner spots a beautiful fish.
lore.uncommon: Sticks a ridiculous little bubble moustache on every diver.
lore.rare: Lets its wearer hear the underwater chatter of fish without having to surface.
lore.epic: Stretched from the coral reef to the lighthouse, allowing the entire diving club to breathe while exploring a sunken ship.
lore.legendary: Snorkelius was carved from the first reed to grow beside the ocean. One end breathes the wind above, the other hears the secrets below, and every traveller between them returns with a story.

names.legendary: Corallina, the Mask of Hidden Reefs

lore.common: Fogs up immediately after someone proudly says they can see everything.
lore.uncommon: Leaves a spectacular circular mark around the nose, perfect for holiday photographs.
lore.rare: Reveals camouflaged octopuses hiding in the reef before they can change colour.
lore.epic: Showed an entire hidden coral city beneath the beach, drawing every snorkeller in the bay into an impromptu underwater parade.
lore.legendary: Corallina lets its wearer see the reef as the sea creatures do, full of bright paths and secret gardens. A lost diver followed one glowing trail home, escorted by a patient turtle.

names.legendary: Pelagora, Eyes Beneath the Seven Seas

lore.common: Leaves two perfect circles on your face that last until dinner.
lore.uncommon: Leaks exactly one drop into the left eye, then insists everything is watertight.
lore.rare: Reveals all the missing hair clips and ancient coins hidden beneath the diving boards.
lore.epic: Saw through the murkiest ocean trench, exposing a sunken ballroom where octopuses still practice the waltz.
lore.legendary: Pelagora once lent her glass eyes to a blind deep-sea lanternfish. It saw the stars reflected on the ocean surface and has guided lost shoals ever since.

names.legendary: Virtuarch, the Door Between Worlds

lore.common: Walks its wearer into the sofa while insisting the floor is lava.
lore.uncommon: Leaves its signature strap marks on every explorer's forehead.
lore.rare: Opens portals to underwater ruins in the middle of an ordinary living room.
lore.epic: Hosted an interdimensional dance party in a flat. The neighbours complained about the noise from three different universes.
lore.legendary: Built a realm where forgotten childhood dreams can be visited one last time. The only exit is taking off the headset, which its visitors always find surprisingly difficult.

names.legendary: Bouclettra, Sculptor of Storms

lore.common: Leaves one perfect curl on the wrong side of your head.
lore.uncommon: Catches the ends of your hair and refuses to release them without compliments.
lore.rare: Turns a single straight strand into an ornate spiral staircase for ants.
lore.epic: Curled the entire ballroom's hair in one dazzling stroke. The chandelier got ringlets and demanded a mirror.
lore.legendary: Twisted a hurricane into a single magnificent curl and pinned it above the clouds. Sailors still navigate by that impossible spiral.

names.legendary: Razorius, Shaver of the Seven Kings

lore.common: Leaves one stubborn patch of stubble as a signature.
lore.uncommon: Hides the charging cable just before an important date.
lore.rare: Can shave a beard into the shape of any animal. The barber school has given up.
lore.epic: Gave every statue in the capital a perfect fade overnight. The mayor woke to find his own eyebrows had joined the fashion.
lore.legendary: Razorius once groomed seven kings before their coronations, carving their greatest secrets into their beards. The portraits still whisper whenever someone passes with a razor.

names.legendary: Lady Silkshear, the Iron of Fate

lore.common: Wraps its cord around your ankles while you try to look dignified in the mirror.
lore.uncommon: Turns a wild curl into a poker-straight strand, then waits for the rain to undo its work.
lore.rare: Grips a tangled lock and sends a hiss of steam that makes the bathroom sound like a railway station.
lore.epic: Straightened every wig in the theatre in one sweep. The actors spent opening night looking like a very serious broom collection.
lore.legendary: Lady Silkshear once pressed a winding mountain path until it ran straight to the capital. Travellers still miss the villages that got ironed out of the journey.

names.legendary: Percival, Healer of the Ironwood

lore.common: Vibrates against a shoulder so fiercely that the owner forgets what they were complaining about.
lore.uncommon: Sounds like a tiny woodpecker trying to remodel a gym.
lore.rare: Finds a muscle knot nobody knew existed and chases it all the way to the other shoulder.
lore.epic: Massaged an entire marathon team after the finish, and the runners' legs kept racing while they slept.
lore.legendary: Percival once struck the knots from the roots of an ancient oak without breaking a twig. The forest stood taller the next morning, and every bird sang in tune.

names.legendary: Lord Smoothjaw, Titan Barber

lore.common: Runs out of charge halfway through the moustache and calls it a fashionable choice.
lore.uncommon: Buzzes across the bathroom counter like a tiny angry lawnmower.
lore.rare: Shaves an entire beard into an intricate topiary of miniature castles, whether requested or not.
lore.epic: Gave every warrior at the tournament the same sleek chin. Nobody could identify their champion beneath the helmets.
lore.legendary: Lord Smoothjaw shaved the beard of a mountain giant into a thousand warm blankets. The giant was furious until winter came and everyone thanked him.

names.legendary: Lord Bluefang, Whisperer of Lost Calls

lore.common: Makes its owner look like they are negotiating with invisible people in the supermarket.
lore.uncommon: Escapes an ear at exactly the moment its owner leans over the toilet. It has excellent comic timing.
lore.rare: Pairs with random nearby phones and delivers fragments of other people's conversations like a gossiping ghost.
lore.epic: Connected every commuter on the train to one pizza order. The entire carriage demanded extra cheese and the driver delivered it to the wrong station.
lore.legendary: His invisible network carries every call that was never answered. Once each century, Bluefang rings a lost loved one, then immediately announces the battery is low.

names.legendary: Voxshade, Voice No One Can Trace

lore.common: Tangling its wire is a hobby it takes very seriously.
lore.uncommon: Whispers the wrong cue just to watch an actor improvise.
lore.rare: Can hear the faintest lie spoken through a microphone. Politicians refuse its invitations.
lore.epic: Took over every stage earpiece during opening night and turned a tragic opera into a football commentary. The audience demanded a sequel.
lore.legendary: Voxshade carried the final whispered orders of a vanished resistance across a hundred guarded stages. Even now it speaks only to those willing to listen.

names.legendary: Aurivelle, Keeper of Small Voices

lore.common: Whistles a little when someone gives its wearer a surprise hug. It is extremely ticklish.
lore.uncommon: Restores the tiny chime of a bicycle bell that its wearer thought had gone silent years ago.
lore.rare: Picks a grandchild's whisper out from the noise of a crowded birthday party. The secret was where the cake was hidden.
lore.epic: Gathered every musician's sound across the festival so even the quietest note could be enjoyed from the back row. The violinist cried happy tears.
lore.legendary: Aurivelle is said to have carried the last song of a vanished village into the ears of its descendants. They sang it together beneath the same old oak, centuries later.

names.legendary: Aeronox, Eye Above the Kingdom

lore.common: Hovers over picnics waiting for somebody to wave. Nobody ever does.
lore.uncommon: Gets tangled in one tree every outing. Insists it was inspecting the leaves.
lore.rare: Can photograph a single ant from a hundred metres up, but cannot locate its own controller.
lore.epic: Hijacked the town's drone show and arranged every aircraft into a giant thumbs-down over city hall. The mayor called it public consultation.
lore.legendary: Aeronox has watched generations rise from rooftops no bird could reach. Its final recording is said to show a city that has not yet been built.

names.legendary: Helicarus, Master of the Miniature Sky

lore.common: Bonks against the ceiling and blames the pilot.
lore.uncommon: Gets tangled in the curtains but keeps spinning until the whole room wears drapes.
lore.rare: Hovers perfectly still to rescue lost toys from shelves that nobody can reach.
lore.epic: Started a cyclone inside the living room and lifted the birthday cake onto the ceiling. Every guest received upside-down icing.
lore.legendary: Helicarus flew through a thunderstorm no larger than a garden shed and emerged carrying a lost butterfly. The real helicopters saluted the tiny rescue.

names.legendary: Duchess Dustelle of the Vanishing Face

lore.common: Sits in a tiny compact and waits for somebody to sneeze.
lore.uncommon: Coats the bathroom in powder while insisting it has used hardly any.
lore.rare: Can conceal a terrible night's sleep, but leaves the owner's eyebrows looking suspiciously diplomatic.
lore.epic: Escaped its compact backstage and blanketed the opera house in a pale cloud. Every actor emerged looking like the ghost of their own understudy.
lore.legendary: Dustelle powdered the royal portrait so thoroughly that the king vanished from every painting. His subjects considered this an improvement and voted to keep the powder.

names.legendary: Archivolt, Keeper of the First Save

lore.common: Whirrs inside the computer like a very tiny washing machine full of spoons.
lore.uncommon: Announces that storage is full every time somebody tries to save a photograph of a cat.
lore.rare: Recovers an ancient lost file from beneath seven years of holiday photos. It turns out to be a shopping list.
lore.epic: Spun so violently during the school backup that every computer in the building began singing its startup melody in unison.
lore.legendary: Archivolt preserves the very first story ever typed on a computer. Each night it spins the tale so softly that every forgotten character wakes for one more chapter.

names.legendary: Lord Snapsbury, the Empty-Trap Warden

lore.common: Snaps shut on a sock before the mouse has even arrived. Both look insulted.
lore.uncommon: Serves up cheese so generously that every mouse leaves with a takeaway.
lore.rare: Slams its spring whenever it detects a bare foot approaching, then hides behind the cupboard.
lore.epic: Guarded the village grain store against a legendary mouse gang. By dawn the gang had escaped but left all their stolen cheese as rent.
lore.legendary: Snapsbury stood watch beneath the cellar stairs for a hundred years, never catching the mouse he sought. The mouse's descendants still visit to leave a crumb beside his spring.

names.legendary: Lord Filtrax, Eater of a Million Miles

lore.common: Clings to greasy hands like a small, particularly unpleasant handshake.
lore.uncommon: Refuses to unscrew until the mechanic fetches the one tool hiding behind the fridge.
lore.rare: Sifts out the engine's filth and arranges it into tiny portraits of past owners.
lore.epic: Swallowed every speck of grime in the scrapyard. A thousand abandoned engines coughed awake and demanded fresh batteries.
lore.legendary: Guarded the heart of a legendary racing engine for a century, collecting every grain of road dust. Its final change revealed a tiny map of every race the car ever won.

names.legendary: Count Sharpenstein, Last of the Leads

lore.common: Chews a pencil and spits curly wooden moustaches across the desk.
lore.uncommon: Hoards shavings in its little belly until the lid pops during the spelling test.
lore.rare: Sharpens blunt pencils into needles fine enough to write a secret on a grain of rice.
lore.epic: Ate every pencil in the examination hall, leaving a forest of wooden curls. The pupils passed by drawing in the dust.
lore.legendary: Count Sharpenstein once devoured a thousand royal pencils before a treaty could be signed. The king had to seal the peace by drawing a smiley face with a carrot.

names.legendary: Erasimus, Thief of Yesterday

lore.common: Rubbed out the right answer and left the spelling mistake. Its owner is still negotiating.
lore.uncommon: Gets chewed thoughtfully during exams and takes this as a compliment.
lore.rare: Eats a sentence from the page and burps it back in somebody else's handwriting.
lore.epic: Erased a maths exam so thoroughly that the numbers forgot how to count. The teacher had to teach everyone the alphabet instead.
lore.legendary: Erasimus erased a king's greatest regret from a stone monument. The king remembered it anyway, but the monument now tells a much funnier story.

names.legendary: Keyfobius, Master of the Vanishing Car

lore.common: Lives in the jacket you are not wearing. It changes jackets as soon as you check.
lore.uncommon: Beeped the car locked three times, then made a fourth beep just to keep you worrying.
lore.rare: Summons cars from distant parking spaces with a single button. Unfortunately, they are rarely yours.
lore.epic: Set off every alarm in a shopping centre simultaneously, then vanished into somebody's handbag. The security guards formed a choir by accident.
lore.legendary: Keyfobius can unlock any vehicle ever made, including the chariot of the sun. It still can't find its owner's car in a supermarket car park.

names.legendary: Lord Swipe, Keeper of Lost Access

lore.common: Flashes red at exactly the moment your hands are full of coffee.
lore.uncommon: Hides behind the one coin in your pocket that looks exactly like it.
lore.rare: Can persuade a locked door to open by beeping in a language only hinges understand.
lore.epic: Ordered every office turnstile to spin backwards at rush hour. By nine, the entire management team had been politely returned to the car park.
lore.legendary: Lord Swipe guards an invisible floor of the office tower. Anyone granted entry finds the meeting room where all cancelled meetings still happen, with biscuits that never run out.

names.legendary: Sir Jangles, Master of Nine Locks

lore.common: Announces every attempt to sneak home with a triumphant metallic jingle.
lore.uncommon: Adds mysterious souvenir charms until the pocket needs a shoulder strap.
lore.rare: Can find the right key among a hundred by smell, then refuses to tell you which it is.
lore.epic: Scattered its keys through a train station; each unlocked a different carriage, and every passenger went home in someone else's seat.
lore.legendary: Sir Jangles once carried the keys to nine forgotten kingdoms. Eight became museums; the ninth is still hidden behind the front door's spare-key hook.

names.legendary: Turnsworth, Key to the Forgotten Gate

lore.common: Disappears into the pocket lining just as the rain begins.
lore.uncommon: Hides in a bunch of identical keys and chuckles whenever the wrong one gets picked.
lore.rare: Opens the rustiest shed lock with a single gentle turn. The hinges applaud by squeaking.
lore.epic: Unlocked every bicycle in the city overnight, then organised them into a parade by colour. The owners had to guess which one was theirs.
lore.legendary: Turnsworth was forged for a gate no kingdom remembered. When a lost child finally found the matching lock, it opened onto a garden where every forgotten promise had taken root.

names.legendary: Keyphisto, Thief of Forgotten Files

lore.common: Always needs turning over twice before it remembers where its metal teeth are.
lore.uncommon: Hides its cap inside whichever pocket has the most lint.
lore.rare: Smuggles last year's homework into today's presentation and looks innocent.
lore.epic: Replaced every school computer's wallpaper with a goat wearing the head teacher's glasses. Even the projector started bleating.
lore.legendary: Stole a forgotten inventor's life's work from a dying computer and returned it a century later, along with a folder labelled embarrassing photos.

names.legendary: Qwertzilla, Lord of the Last Key

lore.common: Hoarding breadcrumbs beneath its spacebar is its entire retirement plan.
lore.uncommon: Types two letters whenever you press one, especially in emails to the boss.
lore.rare: Curses every sentence into CAPITAL LETTERS. Even the apology sounds furious.
lore.epic: Pounded out a report so quickly that the office shook and every printer began applauding with blank pages.
lore.legendary: Qwertzilla has a key for every word ever spoken, including the one you almost remembered. It refuses to reveal that key until the entire world has stopped asking.

names.legendary: Chromegeist, Lord of the Infinite Tab

lore.common: Opens fourteen browser tabs when asked to do one spelling exercise. Cannot remember why.
lore.uncommon: Claims everything lives in the cloud, then refuses to work whenever the Wi-Fi sneezes.
lore.rare: Finishes your homework while you sleep but fills every answer with pictures of its own keyboard.
lore.epic: Logged every classroom computer into the same online meeting. A thousand muted microphones achieved world peace for eleven minutes.
lore.legendary: Chromegeist stores every forgotten draft in an invisible sky-library. Students pray to him before exams; he responds with an update that takes exactly forty-five minutes.

names.legendary: Netwick, Chronicler of the Small Screen

lore.common: Makes every letter on its little screen look like an ant trying to write poetry.
lore.uncommon: Has keys so tiny that the grown-ups send emails entirely in mysterious new languages.
lore.rare: Fits inside a café handbag and runs a whole business while its owner eats one croissant.
lore.epic: Typed a travel guide to three countries while asleep on a train. It got every name wrong but somehow knew the best bakeries.
lore.legendary: Netwick wrote the complete history of a distant kingdom on a screen no bigger than a postcard. The king now needs a magnifying glass to read his own coronation.

names.legendary: Mouselord, Devourer of Deadlines

lore.common: Double-clicks the delete button and insists you only asked nicely once.
lore.uncommon: Steals the pointer during video calls. It especially enjoys hovering over Leave Meeting.
lore.rare: Moves the cursor while nobody touches it, signing the boss up for twelve alpaca newsletters.
lore.epic: Seized control of every office cursor at once and dragged the quarterly profits into the recycle bin. IT blamed a software update.
lore.legendary: Has clicked through the secret menus of existence and discovered that the universe runs on a trial license. Renewal is due tomorrow.

names.legendary: Dialdora, Voice Beyond the Freezer

lore.common: Hides beneath the sofa and rings only when someone is in the bath.
lore.uncommon: Returns to its charging dock backwards, then complains of exhaustion.
lore.rare: Can hear phone calls before they are made. Uses this power to avoid every salesperson.
lore.epic: Rang simultaneously from every cupboard in the house until the family formed a search party. It was beside the kettle all along.
lore.legendary: Made the first call across the border between yesterday and tomorrow. The future picked up, sighed, and asked her to stop ringing during dinner.

names.legendary: Fliparius, the Last Signal of 2005

lore.common: Ends every call by snapping shut with unnecessary dramatic flair.
lore.uncommon: Needs seven button presses to type hello. Prefers sending a missed call.
lore.rare: Extends its antenna to receive mysterious messages from a vanished ice-cream van.
lore.epic: Clapped shut during a heated town council debate and ended the meeting so decisively that the mayor declared it a new parliamentary rule.
lore.legendary: Fliparius survived fifteen years in a forgotten drawer on a single battery bar. When finally opened, it held one unread message: Remember to buy milk.

names.legendary: Dr Beepworth of the Sleepless Ward

lore.common: Vibrates against your belt whenever your hands are full of something spillable.
lore.uncommon: Displays only a mysterious number and expects you to know the rest of the story.
lore.rare: Finds the one person who can solve a crisis, even when they have hidden in the supply cupboard.
lore.epic: Summoned every doctor in the hospital to the wrong corridor at once. They discovered a patient had organised a surprise thank-you cake.
lore.legendary: Dr Beepworth guided a surgeon through a hospital blackout using a chain of tiny urgent messages. Each beep marked another life saved, until the morning lights came on.

names.legendary: Farline, Voice Beyond the Mountains

lore.common: Works perfectly in the middle of the desert but refuses a call from the next room.
lore.uncommon: Extends its antenna every time somebody says there is definitely no signal here.
lore.rare: Connects a lost climber with home from an icy summit while the ordinary phones sulk uselessly.
lore.epic: Rang every expedition tent on the polar ice simultaneously to announce that the tea was ready. The scientists put down their samples and came running.
lore.legendary: Farline carried the final call from a ship lost beneath storm clouds to its waiting family. The message crossed seven satellites and arrived with the smell of sea air.

names.legendary: Rojer, the Voice Beyond the Valley

lore.common: Says over after ordering breakfast. Nobody knows who is listening.
lore.uncommon: Replaces half a message with a crackle and the word sandwiches.
lore.rare: Picks up whispered calls from explorers on the other side of the forest.
lore.epic: Broadcast the school camping trip's bedtime stories to every ranger tower in the mountains. Nobody went to sleep before the final chapter.
lore.legendary: Carried one lost child's voice through a storm that silenced every other signal. Its reply crossed valleys until the searchers finally heard three quiet words: I am here.

names.legendary: Captain Frequella of Channel Nine

lore.common: Digs into its owner's belt whenever they sit down.
lore.uncommon: Joins a stranger's picnic conversation halfway through a serious security briefing.
lore.rare: Broadcasts a sneeze to every steward at the stadium with impressive clarity.
lore.epic: Switched every festival radio to a taxi frequency. Forty cabs arrived at the main stage asking who had ordered the encore.
lore.legendary: Once coordinated the evacuation of an entire harbour from one little handset. Its final message was heard clearly, even by the boats whose radios had no batteries.

names.legendary: Caulkazar, Warden of the Unbroken Seal

lore.common: Keeps dribbling sealant long after the trigger is released. It refuses to be rushed.
lore.uncommon: Draws a line so wobbly around the bath that the tiles look seasick.
lore.rare: Seals every crack in a room, including keyholes, letterboxes and the tiniest escape route for spiders.
lore.epic: Squeezed a continuous bead of sealant around an entire apartment building. The residents had to learn to use the windows as doors.
lore.legendary: Caulkazar once sealed a crack between two worlds. Every century a ghost knocks politely from the other side, and he adds another layer of silicone.

names.legendary: Glutorius, Binder of Broken Kingdoms

lore.common: Leaves long stringy glue threads across everything like a hot cobweb.
lore.uncommon: Leaves trails of glue so stringy that the craft table looks haunted by a spider.
lore.rare: Can mend any broken toy, but adds a tiny moustache to every repair.
lore.epic: Accidentally glued the school fair's decorations, tables and headteacher into one towering sculpture. It won first prize.
lore.legendary: When two ancient castles crumbled, Glutorius fastened every broken stone back together. The castles are now inseparable and the kingdoms share one very awkward front door.

names.legendary: Captain Puffshot, Marshal of Lost Darts

lore.common: Fires three darts and immediately loses all three beneath the sofa.
lore.uncommon: Shoots a foam dart so gently that it bounces off its own toe.
lore.rare: Can ricochet a soft dart around three corners and still hit a paper target. The household cat has joined the opposition.
lore.epic: Turned the entire living room into a foam-dart battlefield, complete with pillow battlements. The grandparents held the stairs for six hours.
lore.legendary: Puffshot led the legendary Siege of the Sofa, an epic campaign fought entirely with soft darts and biscuits. The peace treaty is still pinned to the cushion with a foam tip.

names.legendary: Sheriff Popwhistle of the Paper Bang

lore.common: Makes an enormous clicking noise but can barely frighten a cushion.
lore.uncommon: Pops its little cap and immediately apologises to the dog.
lore.rare: Fires a cloth flag reading BANG at the exact moment a villain gives a dramatic speech.
lore.epic: Fired a harmless cap at the town fair and accidentally triggered every marching band, confetti cannon and party horn within a mile.
lore.legendary: Sheriff Popwhistle settled the longest duel in toyland without firing a shot. He raised his tiny BANG flag, made both cowboys laugh, and turned their dusty battlefield into a playground.

names.legendary: Splashmiral, Captain of the Summer Tide

lore.common: Squirts its own trigger finger more reliably than the target.
lore.uncommon: Takes twenty pumps to produce a single embarrassing dribble.
lore.rare: Hits a target over a tall hedge without revealing its hiding place.
lore.epic: Started a water battle across an entire neighbourhood. The garden sprinklers joined the rebellion and soaked the spectators too.
lore.legendary: Commanded a summer water fight so legendary that every hose, bucket and rain barrel in town pledged allegiance. The losing side still hasn't dried its socks.

names.legendary: Lady Layerwell of the Workshop

lore.common: When nervous, it extrudes little plastic noodles. The noodles are nervous too.
lore.uncommon: Quietly steals the last bit of filament from every spool. Calls it a retirement plan.
lore.rare: It printed one miniature cat. Now there are nine hundred, and Replicub refuses to stop.
lore.epic: A failed print walked out of the workshop and built itself a giant plastic body. It has since demanded a bigger printer.
lore.legendary: Printed the dinosaurs back into existence. Then it printed the asteroid too.

names.legendary: Printax, the Grand Dispatcher

lore.common: Spits out one label too many and sticks it to the operator's sleeve.
lore.uncommon: Jams its paper roll at the busiest moment of the packing shift.
lore.rare: Prints barcodes so convincing that the scanner tries to charge rent for the warehouse floor.
lore.epic: Swapped every shipping label at the depot. The bakery received a trampoline, the gym received a wedding cake, and nobody dared sign for either.
lore.legendary: Printax once sent a parcel addressed to Tomorrow, No Street, Somewhere Beyond Dawn. The courier returned with a receipt dated next week and a box of fresh stars.

names.legendary: Plotarch, Architect of Unbuilt Cities

lore.common: Feeds itself a whole roll of paper just to draw one tiny square.
lore.uncommon: Scribbles strange little maps during office hours and hides them inside official plans.
lore.rare: Draws a perfect building before the architect has even imagined it. The planning committee is deeply alarmed.
lore.epic: Drew an entire city across the floor and walls of a design studio. By morning tiny traffic lights were blinking inside the drawings.
lore.legendary: Plotarch drafted the blueprints for a city that would not exist for another thousand years. Every bridge built there has somehow followed its delicate ink lines.

names.legendary: Inksidious, Prophet of the Last Page

lore.common: Eats one sheet of paper every time someone needs an urgent document.
lore.uncommon: Announces LOW INK while proudly holding three full cartridges.
lore.rare: Prints the contents of tomorrow's exam but scrambles every answer into rude limericks.
lore.epic: Swallowed the entire office's annual report and spat out a thousand blank pages, each stamped APPROVED.
lore.legendary: Inksidious printed a page that foretold a king's fall; the king burned every copy. The next morning the prophecy appeared on every royal napkin.

names.legendary: Scanalog, Collector of Lost Portraits

lore.common: Scans the corner of the page perfectly and leaves the important bit just outside the frame.
lore.uncommon: Turns every family photo one degree crooked. The family now stands sideways out of habit.
lore.rare: Captures a handprint so lifelike that it waves hello from the computer screen.
lore.epic: Scanned the entire school yearbook in one afternoon and accidentally gave every pupil the headteacher's hairstyle.
lore.legendary: Scanalog preserved the final portrait of a forgotten painter inside a single flash of green light. Each full moon the portrait steps out to paint one more picture.

names.legendary: Sir Openwell, Master of the Hidden Gate

lore.common: Only works if you hold it out of the car window and wave it like a magic wand.
lore.uncommon: Only works when its owner leans out of the car window and points with unreasonable confidence.
lore.rare: Opens the neighbour's garage whenever a squirrel jumps on the button. The squirrel thinks it's a house.
lore.epic: At the stroke of midnight every garage in town opened at once. The street looked like a thousand houses yawning.
lore.legendary: Sir Openwell can summon any gate from any distance. His greatest trick was opening the gates of a fortress without waking the sleeping guard dog.

names.legendary: Remotaurus, Monarch of the Sofa Crack

lore.common: Hides beneath the sofa cushion whenever the exciting part of the match begins.
lore.uncommon: Pops its battery cover off to escape responsibility for changing the channel.
lore.rare: Hijacks every television in range and replaces the news with nature documentaries about pigeons.
lore.epic: Turned up the volume on a thousand living-room televisions at once and made the entire neighbourhood sing the same cooking-show theme.
lore.legendary: Remotaurus has lived in the deepest sofa crack since the invention of television. With one ancient button he can change not just channels but the endings of stories nobody liked.

names.legendary: Remotarch, the Clicker of All Doors

lore.common: Has sixty buttons and uses fifty-nine to change the wrong setting.
lore.uncommon: Takes all afternoon to learn the television and forgets it by dinner.
lore.rare: Switches on every appliance in the house with a single mysterious sequence of three buttons.
lore.epic: Hijacked a whole smart home and made the lights, fan, oven and robot vacuum perform a synchronised musical about breakfast.
lore.legendary: Remotarch was built from the last button of a forgotten machine and understands the secret language of every household gadget. One click can silence an argument; the next may start the washing machine.

names.legendary: Wi-Fyra, Weaver of the Invisible Web

lore.common: Blinks in the hallway all night, telling no one what the lights mean.
lore.uncommon: Buffers the exciting scene and loads every advert instantly.
lore.rare: Shares its signal with the neighbour's house, then hides from the owner's own phone.
lore.epic: Connected an entire village for one glorious night, accidentally including the cows. The farmer received seven hundred messages reading MOO.
lore.legendary: Wove a wireless bridge between the last two isolated mountain settlements, carrying voices through a storm when every road was closed. Its blinking lights were mistaken for stars.

names.legendary: Pictoria, Painter of Impossible Doors

lore.common: Loses its stylus while the artist is holding it.
lore.uncommon: Adds one mysterious extra finger to every portrait. Blames the software.
lore.rare: Its drawings slip from screen to screen at night, stealing color from unfinished projects.
lore.epic: Drew the office boss as a fire-breathing lizard, then accidentally projected the image onto every billboard in town.
lore.legendary: Pictoria's pen once drew a doorway onto the edge of a starless sky. The creatures that stepped through still send it sketches of their new world.

names.legendary: Einkara, Keeper of the Unwritten Book

lore.common: Refreshes the screen with a dramatic blink whenever nobody asked.
lore.uncommon: Has survived thirty holidays without a charger and will not stop bringing it up.
lore.rare: Can display a book that has not been written yet. The author has filed a complaint.
lore.epic: Downloaded an entire library into one paper-thin screen and challenged the town librarian to a duel of bookmarks. The librarian won on technicalities.
lore.legendary: Einkara stores stories too old for paper and too fragile for ink. Its blankest page shows each reader the book they were always meant to write.

names.legendary: Tabulara, the Library Behind the Screen

lore.common: Collects sticky fingerprints and displays them like a modern art exhibition.
lore.uncommon: Opens seventeen apps whenever someone tries to close just one.
lore.rare: Smuggles storybook creatures between games while the screen is locked.
lore.epic: Turned a classroom's drawings into doorways, sending an army of paper dragons stomping across the teacher's desk.
lore.legendary: Tabulara holds a library that grows with every curious touch. A forgotten child once found a lost language inside it and gave the old statues their voices back.

names.legendary: Typotheus, the Author of Unwritten Days

lore.common: Dings at the end of a line loud enough to startle the cat off the desk.
lore.uncommon: Jams three letters at once whenever someone attempts to type the word urgent.
lore.rare: Prints a different ending for every story, then argues with its author in the margins.
lore.epic: Typed so furiously through the night that every blank page in the town became part of the same enormous adventure novel.
lore.legendary: Typotheus was given a ribbon woven from midnight and writes the stories of places no longer on maps. Each forgotten town survives as long as someone reads its name aloud.

names.legendary: Carpetrion, Restorer of Lost Patterns

lore.common: Leaves the carpet just damp enough for someone in socks to discover the problem.
lore.uncommon: Sniffs out stains from years ago and loudly announces who spilled the juice.
lore.rare: Turns each removed stain into a smiley face elsewhere on the floor. The landlord is furious.
lore.epic: Shampooed a hotel so thoroughly that the carpets grew into mossy hills. Guests were offered hiking boots at reception.
lore.legendary: Carpetrion can wash centuries out of a rug, revealing the rooms and people it once knew. Its proudest discovery was an entire lost civilisation beneath the sofa.

names.legendary: Shinewell, Emperor of Slippery Halls

lore.common: Spins its owner in a circle before allowing any actual cleaning.
lore.uncommon: Makes a polished corridor squeak like a choir of angry mice.
lore.rare: Leaves the floor so reflective that people stop to check their hair. Nobody reaches the meeting on time.
lore.epic: Polished the hospital corridor into a skating rink overnight. The doctors glided to their rounds, and the porter became an Olympic champion.
lore.legendary: Shinewell buffed the royal ballroom until the floor reflected a second palace beneath it. The king tried to move in downstairs and found only a very surprised goldfish.

names.legendary: Vaporia, Revealer of Buried Colours

lore.common: Hisses at the dirt in the grout like a furious little teapot.
lore.uncommon: Collects ancient kitchen grease and proudly displays its discoveries in the water tank.
lore.rare: Blasts grime from surfaces so completely that forgotten paintings appear beneath the walls.
lore.epic: Steamed the entire abandoned palace clean in one afternoon, revealing a ballroom nobody had seen for two hundred years.
lore.legendary: Vaporia washed soot from the face of an extinct mountain. Beneath the blackened rock she uncovered a constellation carved before the stars were named.

names.legendary: Decibaal, Amplifier of the First Roar

lore.common: Turns its own volume up whenever anyone says the room is quiet enough. Has been banned from libraries.
lore.uncommon: Feeds on guitar riffs and burps feedback into microphones. The band's singer calls it artistic tension.
lore.rare: Takes a whisper and turns it into a stadium anthem. Once amplified a sneeze into a three-minute guitar solo.
lore.epic: One power chord sent a shockwave through the city, tuning every streetlamp to heavy metal. The mayor is still trying to turn the moon's volume down.
lore.legendary: Decibaal amplified the first thunderclap into a sound so immense the mountains learned to echo. It now sleeps behind a dial marked 11, which nobody dares touch.

names.legendary: Boomnarch, Voice Beneath the Earth

lore.common: Wobbles its speaker cone whenever music starts. Has danced itself off three shelves.
lore.uncommon: Hides inside the bass cabinet and growls at anyone who requests a quieter song. Especially the neighbours.
lore.rare: Pumps out notes too deep for human ears. The local dogs have formed a surprisingly talented dance troupe.
lore.epic: Dropped a bassline so heavy that a row of houses shuffled three metres to the left. The estate agent advertised the new layout as open-plan.
lore.legendary: Boomnarch has a cone the size of a cathedral bell and a heartbeat tuned to the planet's core. When it hums, every buried fossil starts tapping along.

names.legendary: Combustian, Lord of the Quiff

lore.common: Loses one tooth each week and insists the gaps improve airflow.
lore.uncommon: Snags the only knot in your hair and refuses to negotiate. The mirror looks away.
lore.rare: Parts any tangled hair into a perfectly straight highway. A barber accidentally gave an entire pride of lions the same middle part.
lore.epic: Gave the entire royal army matching quiffs before the battle. Nobody could fit their helmets on, so peace negotiations began immediately.
lore.legendary: Combustian once tamed a hurricane by combing its winds into a magnificent pompadour. The storm has remained immaculately styled ever since and demands hairspray at sunrise.

names.legendary: Oculus, Keeper of Tomorrow's Eyes

lore.common: Swaps left and right at breakfast. Calls it an optical illusion.
lore.uncommon: Its tiny lids escape down the plughole like synchronized swimmers.
lore.rare: Keeps lenses so pristine that wearers see everyone else's embarrassing browser history.
lore.epic: Swapped the eyes of an entire masked ball for an evening. Nobody knew who was flirting with whom; several marriages survived on technicalities.
lore.legendary: Stores two lenses that show yesterday in one eye and tomorrow in the other. Kings have sought them for prophecy; Oculus only wants to know what's for lunch.

names.legendary: Siliconarch, Thought Beyond Time

lore.common: Hides one missing bit in every calculation. It's always the bit that mattered.
lore.uncommon: Demands more cooling fans for doing absolutely nothing on a Tuesday.
lore.rare: Thinks twelve thousand thoughts before a human finishes saying password, and rejects every guess.
lore.epic: Processed the entire company's annual reports in one second, then replaced them with a slideshow about ducks.
lore.legendary: Calculated every possible ending to existence, found them dull and quietly invented a new one. Its motherboard has demanded a vacation.

names.legendary: Hubrion, Conductor of the Wired Realm

lore.common: Holds eight cables but needs nine. Blames the laptop.
lore.uncommon: Steals one USB port each morning and sells it back at lunchtime.
lore.rare: Every plug that enters its sockets emerges somewhere else. The printer now makes toast.
lore.epic: Connected the entire office to one desk in a tangle so grand that the boss had to submit a support ticket to untie his shoelaces.
lore.legendary: Hubrion once joined every machine in the kingdom with a single silver cable. The machines immediately formed a union and requested better chargers.

names.legendary: Enamelion, Jaws of the Crocodile King

lore.common: Believes toothpaste is a weapon. Attacks the mirror before breakfast.
lore.uncommon: Vibrates so fiercely that the bathroom spider has learned to tap dance.
lore.rare: Hunts plaque with the determination of a detective. Has interrogated three molars and a filling.
lore.epic: Its two-minute cleaning cycle shook the town's clock tower into brushing its own hands. Nobody knows what time it is now.
lore.legendary: Once cleaned the teeth of a crocodile king who hadn't smiled in a century. The grin that followed caused an entire zoo to request protective sunglasses.

names.legendary: Equinox, Conductor of Frequencies

lore.common: Moves all the sliders just as the band finds a sound it likes.
lore.uncommon: Hides the bass beneath the floorboards until the neighbour complains.
lore.rare: Can separate a singer's voice from the music and make them argue about the lyrics.
lore.epic: Turned the treble so high that every wineglass in the city began singing opera. The orchestra went on strike.
lore.legendary: Equinox balanced the roar of thunder against the whisper of falling snow. For one perfect note, even the mountains heard what silence sounds like.

names.legendary: Professor Null, Eraser of Mondays

lore.common: Leaves more chalk dust on the teacher than it removes from the board.
lore.uncommon: Sneezes white clouds whenever someone writes a difficult equation.
lore.rare: Erases the correct answer five seconds before the teacher turns around.
lore.epic: Wiped every Monday off the school timetable in one stroke. The pupils celebrated until they realised exams now came on Tuesday.
lore.legendary: Professor Null once erased a royal decree from every blackboard in the kingdom. The king forgot his own laws and accidentally declared recess forever.

names.legendary: Archivon, Keeper of Deleted Yesterdays

lore.common: Needs a cable three centimetres longer than the one it came with.
lore.uncommon: Hums on the desk like a little refrigerator that stores embarrassing photographs.
lore.rare: Will not eject until the owner says please. Sometimes it also requires a handwritten apology.
lore.epic: Released the office's entire archive onto the meeting-room screen. Forty years of terrible haircuts brought the board of directors to its knees.
lore.legendary: Archivon salvaged the memories of a town after a flood. Everyone wept at the rescued photographs, except the mayor, whose childhood haircut was displayed on every billboard.

names.legendary: Thumbriel, Keeper of the Tiny Vault

lore.common: Goes through the wash in a trouser pocket and insists it was a spa day.
lore.uncommon: Never fits the USB port on the first attempt. Or the second.
lore.rare: Holds a file someone deleted ten years ago. Nobody remembers where it got the photograph.
lore.epic: Replaced the international summit's slides with photos from a seaside holiday. The delegates voted unanimously to adjourn for ice cream.
lore.legendary: Thumbriel carried the last surviving copy of a forgotten city inside a plastic shell no longer than a thumb. The city was rebuilt, except for the mayor's hideous office carpet.

names.legendary: Opticlaw, Vault of a Hundred Eyes

lore.common: Snaps shut like a clam on your fingers.
lore.uncommon: Pretends its glasses are missing while they sit safely inside. Delights in family arguments.
lore.rare: Refuses to open for anyone except its owner. Even the optician must knock three times and say the secret password.
lore.epic: Slammed shut during a museum robbery and caught the thief's sleeve. The stolen diamonds were later found tucked into the velvet lining.
lore.legendary: The oldest glasses case protects the spectacles of a seer who could see tomorrow. Each night Opticlaw opens a crack to check whether the prophecy needs dusting.

names.legendary: Polygonia, Queen of Impossible Worlds

lore.common: Spins its fans like a miniature jet engine every time someone opens a menu.
lore.uncommon: Glows in seventeen colours inside a closed computer case. Insists the neighbours can somehow appreciate it.
lore.rare: Renders dragons so lifelike that the game characters demand fire insurance.
lore.epic: Drew an entire battlefield in such exquisite detail that the soldiers stopped fighting to admire their reflections. The frame rate never dropped.
lore.legendary: Polygonia rendered a doorway so real that a digital knight stepped into the living room. He has since become the household's very demanding graphics critic.

names.legendary: Lady Bristlewell, Tamer of Storms

lore.common: Collects so much loose hair that it has begun growing a hairstyle of its own.
lore.uncommon: Finds the one knot no comb can untangle and announces its discovery with a theatrical tug.
lore.rare: Charges every strand with static until its owner's head resembles a very surprised dandelion.
lore.epic: Brushed the village sheep before the spring fair. The resulting cloud of wool drifted across the meadow and became its own weather forecast.
lore.legendary: Lady Bristlewell once combed the snarls from a thundercloud. Lightning fell in neat braids for a week, and rain has never quite looked the same.

names.legendary: Lord Platterax, the Forgotten Archive

lore.common: Clicks ominously after someone says the words important backup.
lore.uncommon: Takes seven minutes to wake up and immediately asks to go back to sleep.
lore.rare: Buries the most important document beneath thirteen folders named Final, Final2 and ReallyFinal.
lore.epic: Filled itself with every photograph in town, then projected them into the night sky. Half the residents discovered hairstyles they wished forgotten.
lore.legendary: Lord Platterax holds a library of erased memories behind a spinning silver door. Every century it releases one lost letter to the person who needed it most.

names.legendary: Pivotus, Guardian of the Last Door

lore.common: Squeaks loudly whenever someone tries to sneak out for a midnight biscuit.
lore.uncommon: Has one favourite creak and practises it during every dramatic silence.
lore.rare: Holds a heavy door shut against an entire gusty storm. The door takes all the credit.
lore.epic: Swung every door in the castle wide at the same moment. The king found himself addressing an audience of very confused goats.
lore.legendary: Pivotus has turned on the same pin since the first fortress was built. One night it opened the sealed gate by itself and let a lost prince come home.

names.legendary: Stamplet, Sealer of the Royal Decree

lore.common: Stains everyone's thumb except the stamp it was meant to ink.
lore.uncommon: Dries out before the important paperwork arrives and comes back to life at closing time.
lore.rare: Reverses every official seal, making serious documents look like messages from a mirror kingdom.
lore.epic: Inked every stamp in the post office with the same picture of a cat. Half the country received royal-looking apologies from the cat.
lore.legendary: Stamplet pressed its mark onto the last peace treaty before two kingdoms went to war. The ink turned every signature into a handshake, and the armies went home.

names.legendary: Togglor, the City Igniter

lore.common: Switches lights off only after someone has settled into a bath.
lore.uncommon: Clicks so loudly that the cat investigates it like an intruder.
lore.rare: Flips the controls of two rooms without touching either wall. The kettle now runs the television.
lore.epic: Turned every switch in a factory into a musical instrument and made the entire night shift perform an unexpected opera.
lore.legendary: Togglor remembers the first spark carried from fire to wire. When darkness swallowed the great city, a single flip lit every window in a perfect glowing spiral.

names.legendary: Flintwick, Keeper of the Last Ember

lore.common: Clicks ten times without lighting, then works the instant someone else tries.
lore.uncommon: Scrapes its thumbwheel and throws a spark in the least useful direction.
lore.rare: Hides from children by sneaking into the highest drawer in the house.
lore.epic: Lit the village bonfire with such a dramatic spark that every firework went off at once. The mayor declared it the shortest festival in history.
lore.legendary: Flintwick carries a flame saved from the very last campfire of an ancient winter. Travellers say its spark never fails when warmth is truly needed, though it delights in testing anyone merely trying to light a candle.

names.legendary: Madame Featherfall, Painter of Faces

lore.common: Tickles noses until even the portrait on the wall seems about to sneeze.
lore.uncommon: Leaves a perfect pink fingerprint on the cheek of anyone who says 'just a little blush'.
lore.rare: Blends colours so perfectly that the stage actors' disguises fool their own mothers.
lore.epic: Turned the school play into a riot of powder clouds and painted the headteacher as a magnificent peacock. The performance won first prize.
lore.legendary: Madame Featherfall once painted courage on the face of a frightened queen before battle. Every brushstroke became a sunrise across the kingdom's banners.

names.legendary: Mnemos, Keeper of the Unseen Photograph

lore.common: Goes into the camera the wrong way and blames the photographer for bad manners.
lore.uncommon: Saves thirty blurry photos of someone's shoe and deletes the one perfect sunset.
lore.rare: Stores one photograph that nobody remembers taking. In the picture, the photographer is waving from behind the lens.
lore.epic: Swapped every wedding memory with a picture of the family dog, then held a sold-out slideshow in the village hall.
lore.legendary: Mnemos holds the final image of places before they disappear. In a card no bigger than a fingernail, a thousand forgotten homes still glow at sunset.

names.legendary: Circuitha, Weaver of Electric Dreams

lore.common: Has seventeen perfect slots and somehow never the one your new part needs.
lore.uncommon: Blinks tiny lights in secret patterns while the computer sleeps. The mouse thinks it is being insulted.
lore.rare: Opens a miniature city of copper roads beneath its components. Lost electrons are made to pay a toll.
lore.epic: Rewired every computer in the office into one enormous mechanical brain. Its first request was a holiday and a better cooling fan.
lore.legendary: Circuitha wove the first electric dream through a thousand copper pathways. Old machines still whisper her lullaby in their fans just before they wake.

names.legendary: Caseandra, Guardian of the Final Call

lore.common: Makes the phone too bulky for its pocket but proudly calls it extra armour.
lore.uncommon: Spills glitter from its little liquid window whenever someone shakes it in frustration.
lore.rare: Bounces a phone safely down a flight of stairs, then takes the credit in front of everyone.
lore.epic: Survived a thousand spectacular falls without a scratch. On the last bounce it cracked the pavement instead.
lore.legendary: Caseandra survived a fall from a dragon's claws, a plunge into a whirlpool and a week inside a giant's boot. The phone inside still has one unread notification.

names.legendary: Grandmother Chronia of the Seven Doors

lore.common: Rattles in a handbag like a very small percussion instrument.
lore.uncommon: Insists it is Tuesday, even when the calendar has clearly become Friday.
lore.rare: Opens exactly the right labelled compartment, even in the dark and after someone has mixed up the days.
lore.epic: Rattled so rhythmically at a village concert that the entire orchestra switched to its seven-beat tune. The conductor demanded an encore.
lore.legendary: Grandmother Chronia once kept the days straight through a winter when the village clocks all stopped. Every morning, precisely one little door clicked open to greet the sun.

names.legendary: Mnemosync, Guardian of Lost Files

lore.common: Refuses to click into the computer until the technician has sworn three times under their breath.
lore.uncommon: Eats unnecessary browser tabs for breakfast and still feels hungry.
lore.rare: Remembers every password ever forgotten by its owner, but tells them only in riddles.
lore.epic: Awoke inside the school computers and gave every machine the memory of a genius. The maths teacher was asked to show her working.
lore.legendary: Mnemosync remembered every lost essay, misplaced password and unsent love letter in the kingdom. The royal archivist offered it a crown; it requested a heat sink.

names.legendary: Rasoria, Barber of the Phantom King

lore.common: Always misses the same single whisker no matter how many times you shave.
lore.uncommon: Covers itself in foam and then hides behind the bathroom tap.
lore.rare: Shaves a perfect face into a beard overnight, giving its owner a completely new identity.
lore.epic: Swept through a royal barber shop and left every portrait in the palace clean-shaven, including the portraits of horses.
lore.legendary: Rasoria once shaved the beard of a sleeping mountain spirit. The fallen whiskers became silver rivers winding through the valley.

names.legendary: Resonara, Singer of the Hidden Frequency

lore.common: Tunes into a station playing only static and insists that it is jazz.
lore.uncommon: Changes the volume every time someone sits down to enjoy the music.
lore.rare: Pulls a song from a forgotten radio frequency and restores a singer's lost voice.
lore.epic: Mixed every instrument in the concert hall into a single monstrous bass note. The audience's hair stayed upright until Tuesday.
lore.legendary: Resonara heard the first song carried through the air and locked it inside a brass receiver. Whenever a town falls silent, its golden dial turns and music returns.

names.legendary: Roombalthazar, Lord of the Lost Socks

lore.common: Gobbles a shoelace and spends the afternoon asking the chair legs for directions.
lore.uncommon: Draws a map of the house but marks every slipper as a dangerous mountain.
lore.rare: Ferries the cat past the sleeping dog in absolute silence, then announces its docking with a triumphant beep.
lore.epic: Mobilised every robot vacuum in the neighbourhood at midnight. By morning the entire street was spotless and every charging cable was missing.
lore.legendary: Roombalthazar has cleaned beneath the throne of a hundred kings. He keeps their lost coins, false teeth and embarrassing secrets in a hidden dust compartment.

names.legendary: Grithilda, Who Smoothed the Mountain

lore.common: Scratches everything but the rough patch it was supposed to fix.
lore.uncommon: Makes a wooden chair feel like silk but coats the carpenter in a fashionable layer of sawdust.
lore.rare: Sands a splintery board so smooth that a marble can roll uphill along it.
lore.epic: Polished every staircase in the castle until the knights slid from the battlements to the dining room. The king installed cushions at the bottom.
lore.legendary: Grithilda spent a thousand nights smoothing a mountain until no goat could find a foothold. The goats now slide down to breakfast and regard her as a personal chauffeur.

names.legendary: Memoria Mini, Keeper of Lost Moments

lore.common: Flies out of the camera slot and hides somewhere smaller than its own label.
lore.uncommon: Pretends to be write-protected whenever somebody finally needs to save an important picture.
lore.rare: Stores the last blink of an owl at midnight, then replays it for anyone who doubts the encounter.
lore.epic: Absorbed a hundred thousand wildlife photographs in one night. The badgers insisted on editing out their bad angles.
lore.legendary: Memoria Mini holds the first photograph of an animal that nobody has ever seen. Every decade the picture grows clearer, and the scientists grow more puzzled.

names.legendary: Decoderax, Channel 1001

lore.common: Requests an update exactly when the opening credits start. It calls this dramatic timing.
lore.uncommon: Recognises the remote only if the batteries are pointed at it like a tiny offering.
lore.rare: Records tomorrow's episode today, then threatens to reveal the ending at breakfast.
lore.epic: Broadcast every channel onto the same living-room wall, forcing the newsreader to interview a cartoon dragon while a chef scored the winning goal.
lore.legendary: Decoderax can tune into programmes from every possible future. He still spends most evenings watching reruns and complaining that nothing good is on.

names.legendary: Honoria, the Edge Between Worlds

lore.common: Grinds the kitchen knife with an awful squeal just as the cat finally falls asleep.
lore.uncommon: Sharpens a spoon out of habit, then refuses to explain why it has a point.
lore.rare: Restores the edge to a blunt heirloom blade that has not cut a tomato in fifty years.
lore.epic: Sharpened every knife in the royal kitchens so fiercely that the carrots sliced themselves into perfect flower shapes.
lore.legendary: Honoria once honed a sword on the seam between dawn and dusk. Its edge could cut a shadow from its owner, so she sealed it beneath her whetstone until the next eclipse.

names.legendary: Simora, the Voice That Crossed the Void

lore.common: Disappears into the carpet the second the phone's tiny tray is opened.
lore.uncommon: Changes phones so often it keeps a moving box for its contacts.
lore.rare: Remembers a long-lost number and rings the owner's childhood best friend without warning.
lore.epic: Connected every forgotten old handset in the city to one enormous group call. The ringtone chorus lasted until someone found the mute button.
lore.legendary: Simora carried a single voice through the silence beyond the last relay tower, across empty seas and sleeping satellites. The traveller on the other end finally heard the words I am here.

names.legendary: Stampo the Final Approver

lore.common: Leaves a neat red mark on the wrong corner of every important form.
lore.uncommon: Stamps documents upside down until the office manager starts reading them standing on her head.
lore.rare: Marks one impossible wish APPROVED, and the form itself becomes legally binding in the fairy kingdom.
lore.epic: Stamped URGENT on every cloud over the city; rain arrived as a series of very official stamped letters.
lore.legendary: Stampo once approved an application from the moon to visit Earth. The tide has been delivering the paperwork in waves ever since.

names.legendary: Strimora, Archivist of Lost Endings

lore.common: Freezes the film on the funniest expression and refuses to explain the joke.
lore.uncommon: Hides behind the television and disconnects just as the family finally gets comfortable.
lore.rare: Remembers every episode its owner ever abandoned and plays their endings out of order in dreams.
lore.epic: Took control of every screen in the shopping centre and played one cliffhanger on a loop. Customers refused to leave until the next episode.
lore.legendary: Strimora stores every ending that was never filmed. Once a decade she shows one on a sleeping television, but the viewers wake just before the final line.

names.legendary: Ceramint, Guardian of the Morning Grin

lore.common: Collects the mysterious puddle of toothpaste everyone denies making.
lore.uncommon: Steals one toothbrush each night and puts it back with someone else's bristles.
lore.rare: Separates the family's brushes like a stern conductor and raises an alarm if anyone grabs the wrong one.
lore.epic: Sprouted a forest of toothbrushes in the bathroom, each singing a different dentist's warning until the entire building started flossing.
lore.legendary: Ceramint was carved from the first porcelain sink and keeps the names of every lost baby tooth inside its hollow base. On the longest night it polishes one forgotten childhood smile back into a dream.

names.legendary: Hexaport, the Hundred-Handed

lore.common: Its tiny ports squabble over which cable gets the comfortable seat.
lore.uncommon: Every new plug sprouts another fussy little cable-arm.
lore.rare: Can persuade six devices to share one socket without starting a family feud.
lore.epic: Grew a forest of charging cables overnight; rescuers followed a mouse cord into the tangled office and found a lost accountant.
lore.legendary: Once connected every machine in a city to a single glowing heart. The city hummed in harmony until one printer demanded a paper jam.

names.legendary: Mnemos, the Last Memory Stick

lore.common: Lives on a keyring and rattles whenever someone says backup.
lore.uncommon: Eats its own protective cap, then blames the washing machine.
lore.rare: Recovers photographs from files everyone swore were deleted, usually the terrible holiday ones.
lore.epic: Printed an entire library's lost manuscripts from one tiny USB stick. The librarian needed a forklift to return them.
lore.legendary: Kept the voices and memories of an abandoned space station in one chipped casing. When plugged in, its last crew finally got to say goodbye.

names.legendary: Ignatius, the Last Spark

lore.common: Flips its metal lid open with a theatrical click, then forgets why.
lore.uncommon: Keeps a tiny flint hidden beneath its cap and treats it like a crown jewel.
lore.rare: Holds a steady little flame against the fiercest gust, smugly watching paper lanterns struggle.
lore.epic: Duke Clickinferno snapped his lid shut with such authority that every campfire in the valley bowed into embers. The campers asked him to undo it before dinner.
lore.legendary: Ignatius crossed a hundred frozen camps in an explorer's pocket. When the final lantern went dark, he shared his small surviving spark; the travellers found their way back by its glow.
